title: Rational fixed flags and scalar extension of a split Borel pair
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $H$ be a reductive $F$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth affine of finite type, geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure. Let $T\subseteq B\subseteq H$ with $T$ a split maximal torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] and $B$ a split solvable Borel subgroup [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure, def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. A Borel is a smooth connected closed subgroup maximal among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups. Split solvable means that there is a finite series of smooth connected closed subgroups normal in their predecessor, with successive fppf quotients $\mathbf G_a$ or $\mathbf G_m$. Suppose $Q$ represents the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/B(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $F$-algebras. For every field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], $T_L$ is a split maximal torus of $H_L$ and $B_L$ is a split solvable Borel subgroup of $H_L$. Let $N_H(T)$ denote the subgroup scheme whose points normalize $T$ after every algebra extension, and let $W=N_H(T)/T$ be its fppf quotient. Then $W$ is a finite constant group scheme, and the map $N_H(T)(L)\to W(L)$ is surjective for every $L/F$. Put $I=W(F)$; the map $W(F)\to W(L)$ is a bijection. Choose $n_w\in N_H(T)(F)$ representing each $w\in I$. The subfunctor $Q^T$ of $Q$ whose $A$-points are those $x\in Q(A)$ fixed by all $t\in T(A')$ after every commutative $A$-algebra extension $A'$ is represented by the closed subscheme
$$\coprod_{w\in I}\operatorname{Spec}F\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ Q^T,\qquad w\longmapsto n_wB.$$
For every $L/F$ the same points $n_{w,L}B_L$ give the entire fixed subscheme $(Q_L)^{T_L}$ as a disjoint union of reduced $L$-points. If $H=T$, then $W$ is trivial and $Q^T=Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$.

source.place: Chapter 21 standing arbitrary field, printed p.424; Proposition 21.1, p.424 (constant Weyl group and rational representatives); Summary 21.41, p.436; the fixed-scheme paragraph immediately before Proposition 21.70, p.446. Scalar-extension stability of split Borel pairs is used throughout Section 21h. The fixed-scheme assertion is scheme-theoretic, not just a statement about rational points.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension], $T_L$ is maximal for every $L/F$; the given product decomposition of $T$ base changes, so it is split. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-solvable-cocharacter-containment] to $V=B$, obtaining a regular $F$-cocharacter $\lambda$ and $B\subseteq P_\lambda$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry], regularity gives $Z_\lambda=T$ and $P_\lambda=U_\lambda\rtimes T$ with $U_\lambda$ split unipotent. Concatenate a coordinate split series of $T$ (taking preimages in $P_\lambda$) with a split series of $U_\lambda$; thus $P_\lambda$ is smooth connected solvable. Maximality of $B$ forces $B=P_\lambda$. These limit subgroups commute with field extension. The weight decomposition of the tangent representation tensors with a field extension, so the nonzero weights and regularity of $\lambda$ are unchanged. Over an algebraic closure of any $L$, [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] makes $(B_L)_{\overline L}=P_{\lambda_{\overline L}}$ a Borel. To verify maximality over $L$ as maximality among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups, any smooth connected solvable $V\supseteq B_L$ lies in some regular $P_\mu$ by the containment input over $L$. Over $\overline L$ the inclusion $P_\lambda\subseteq P_\mu$ is an inclusion of Borels, hence equality; faithful scalar extension reflects equality of their defining ideals. Consequently $V=B_L$. The displayed split series of $P_\lambda$ also base changes, proving the required split solvability.

source.place: Chapter 21 opening, p.424; Proposition 21.29 and Theorem 21.32, pp.433-435; Theorem 13.33, pp.265-266.

proof.text: Write $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ for the given splitting. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $G=H$ (smooth affine of finite type over a field, hence of finite presentation): the centralizer $C$ and the normalizer $N=N_H(T)$ are smooth closed subgroup schemes, and $N$ is covered by the open and closed subschemes $N_\sigma$, $\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbf Z)$, on which conjugation $t\mapsto gtg^{-1}$ is the monomial automorphism $\sigma$. Over a field distinct $\sigma$ give distinct automorphisms, so the $N_\sigma$ are pairwise disjoint and $N=\coprod_\sigma N_\sigma$. As $N$ is of finite type over $F$, its space is Noetherian with finitely many connected components, so the set $J$ of $\sigma$ with $N_\sigma\ne\varnothing$ is finite. Conjugation by $gh$ is conjugation by $h$ followed by $g$, so $N_\sigma N_\tau\subseteq N_{\sigma\tau}$, $N_\sigma^{-1}=N_{\sigma^{-1}}$, $N_1=C$, and $J$ is a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbf Z)$. Since $T$ is geometrically maximal (step 1), [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] gives $C=T$. For $\sigma\in J$, $N_\sigma$ is a nonempty open subscheme of the smooth $N$, hence smooth and surjective over $\operatorname{Spec}F$, so faithfully flat of finite presentation; and $(d,t)\mapsto(d,dt)$ is an isomorphism $N_\sigma\times_FT\to N_\sigma\times_FN_\sigma$ with inverse $(d,d')\mapsto(d,d^{-1}d')$, because $d^{-1}d'\in N_1=T$. Thus each $N_\sigma$ is a right $T$-torsor. The label map $N\to\coprod_{\sigma\in J}\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a group homomorphism, fppf locally surjective (each $N_\sigma\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is an fppf cover), and two sections with the same label differ by a unique section of $T$. Sheafifying the coset presheaf identifies $W=N/T$ with the finite constant group scheme on $J$; no scheme quotient is assumed in advance.

source.place: Proposition 21.1, p.424, and its definition of the Weyl group; Corollaries 12.40 and 13.10; the normalizer loci of Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 2.1.2 and Corollary B.2.7 as recorded in lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer.

proof.text: Let $L/F$. By the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer], $N_L=N_{H_L}(T_L)$ with the same loci $(N_\sigma)_L$; base change of the torsor isomorphism of step 2 makes $(N_\sigma)_L$ a right $T_L$-torsor over $\operatorname{Spec}L$, and $(N_\sigma)_L\ne\varnothing$ exactly for $\sigma\in J$, as surjectivity onto the base is preserved by base change. The split torus is split solvable (its coordinate series has quotients $\mathbf G_m$), so [lem-sfb-split-solvable-torsors-and-variety] trivializes this torsor Zariski locally. An open cover of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ has a member equal to the whole scheme. Thus $(N_\sigma)(L)\ne\varnothing$, proving the surjectivity $N_H(T)(L)\to W(L)$. Maps from the connected scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ to the finite coproduct select precisely one label; hence $W(F)\to W(L)$ is the identity on $J$, in particular bijective. Take $L=F$ and choose one point $n_w$ in each fibre. No multiplicative choice of representatives is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 21.1 proof, p.424; Proposition 16.55(c), p.344, supplies the split-torus torsor triviality (equivalently Corollary 3.47).

proof.text: Put $E=\coprod_{w\in W(F)}\operatorname{Spec}F$, and map its $w$-component to $e_w=n_wB\in Q(F)$. This point is fixed scheme-theoretically: for every test algebra and every $t\in T$, $tn_wB=n_w(n_w^{-1}tn_w)B=n_wB$ because $n_w$ normalizes $T\subseteq B$. If $n'_w$ is another lift, the torsor identity gives $n'_w=n_wt$ for $t\in T(F)$, so its coset is the same. For any $L/F$, the quotient $Q_L$ represents the fppf quotient $H_L/B_L$: on an $L$-algebra the two coset presheaves agree, and an fppf cover by algebras over it automatically respects its $L$-structure. Likewise restricting the fixed-point condition to $L$-algebras gives exactly the $T_L$-fixed condition, since every further algebra extension is again an $L$-algebra.

source.place: Section 21h, paragraph before Proposition 21.70, p.446; quotient and universal fixed-point definitions in the item.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/F$. Step 1 makes $(H_K,T_K,B_K)$ a split Borel pair. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to this pair to obtain its unipotent radical, positive roots and right Borel torsor. The quotient identification in step 4 and the uniqueness of the represented quotient identify $Q_K$ with the flag scheme of [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry]. Step 3 identifies its index $N_H(T)(K)/T(K)$ with $W(F)$, with representatives $n_{w,K}$. That node asserts that the fixed subscheme is precisely the finite disjoint union of these reduced points, on all test algebras. Thus $E_K\to Q_K$ is a closed immersion representing the fixed functor, not merely a bijection of $K$-points. The base change $Q_K\to Q$ is an fpqc covering: a field extension is faithfully flat, and the corresponding map of spectra is affine and surjective, as are its base changes. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion] to conclude that $E\to Q$ is a closed immersion. To check that it represents all fixed points, take $x\in Q^T(A)$. After the faithfully flat cover $A\to A\otimes_F K$, its restriction factors uniquely through $E_K$. The two pullbacks of this factor on the overlap agree, since their composites to $Q$ are the same and $E\to Q$ is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], they descend uniquely to $\operatorname{Spec}A\to E$, whose composite is $x$ by the uniqueness part of that same descent statement. Conversely step 4 makes every point of $E$ fixed. Therefore $E\simeq Q^T$ as functors on all commutative algebras.

source.place: Section 21h before Proposition 21.70, p.446; algebraically closed fixed geometry uses Theorem 13.1, p.254. Descent: Stacks 02L6 (lemma-descending-property-closed-immersion) and 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), descent.tex.

proof.text: For $L/F$, the fixed-functor identity of step 4 gives $(Q_L)^{T_L}=(Q^T)_L=E_L$. Its components are $\operatorname{Spec}L$ and the maps are exactly $n_{w,L}B_L$; in particular they are reduced. If $H=T$, the given inclusions force $B=T$. The quotient sheaf $T/T$ is the singleton sheaf, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}F$; the normalizer quotient is also $T/T$. Thus $W$ is trivial and $Q^T=Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$, including rank zero.
